Operator: Good day, and welcome to the VeriCom Global third quarter Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question at that time, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. For those on webcast, there will be a button to request enrollment. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded. I would now like to turn the call over to Sarah Jenkins, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you, Operator. Good morning, everyone, and welcome to VeriCom Global's third quarter Earnings Conference Call. Joining me on the call today are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Jordan Lee, Chief Financial Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks and uncertainties that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more complete discussion of these risks.

Alex Rivera: Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. I'm pleased to report our results for the third quarter. We achieved total net subscriber additions of 248,000 broadband and mobility revenue generating units, up 12% quarter-over-quarter and 28% year-over-year, which reflects our strong execution in a dynamic market marked by cord-cutting and economic pressures. We are particularly excited about the initial performance of our NexWave Home Ultra 5G fixed wireless access service and its contribution of $212 million in incremental revenue alongside 825,000 broadband subscribers. Our investments in spectrum assets, now at 82% utilization, are also paying off, driving increased customer satisfaction and loyalty through enhanced 5G Standalone deployments. Furthermore, we have focused on our content and media segment, which delivered $2.85 billion in revenue and added 2.8 million paid subscribers, allowing us to maintain profitability with adjusted EBITDA margins expanding to 32.3%. Finally, our strategic focus remains on new product launches like NexStream+ bundles and enterprise 5G private networks, which together drove $478 million in revenue uplift and 1.45 million net adds.

Jordan Lee: Thank you, Alex. Turning to the financials, our revenue for the quarter was $15.2 billion, representing a 9% increase year-over-year on a reported basis and 11% on a constant currency basis. Our adjusted EBITDA was $4.6 billion, with a margin of 30.2%, up 140 basis points from the prior year. We continue to manage our expenses effectively, with content spend held flat as a percentage of revenue at 49%, and are on track to meet our financial targets for the year, including full-year adjusted EBITDA growth of 10-12%. Our capital expenditures were $2.5 billion, primarily driven by investments in our 5G network expansion, fiber-to-the-home rollouts passing 4.2 million homes, and edge computing densification.

Let me now provide more color on our net subscriber additions by segment, which continue to underscore our leadership in the converged telecommunications and media landscape. For the quarter, we delivered total net adds of 248,000 broadband and mobility RGUs, up 12% quarter-over-quarter and a robust 28% year-over-year. This marks our 11th straight quarter of positive net adds across both residential and business segments, defying industry headwinds like cord-cutting pressures and macroeconomic uncertainty.

Starting with residential, we added 212,000 net subscribers—our strongest quarterly performance since Q4 2021. This was driven by a residential broadband net add of 165,000, video of 28,000, and wireless of 19,000. Year-over-year, residential broadband growth accelerated to 35%, fueled by our aggressive FTTH—fiber-to-the-home—rollout, now passing 4.2 million homes with 72% take rates in new-build areas. In the U.S. Northeast and Midwest, where we've deployed over 1,200 miles of new dark fiber in partnership with crown castle providers, we saw triple-digit YoY growth at 142%, capturing share from cable peers like Comcast's Xfinity amid their DOCSIS 3.1 saturation.

On the video side, our VeriStream bundle—integrating our linear TV with FAST channels and third-party SVOD like Peacock and Paramount+—held churn to just 1.1%, down 20 basis points QoQ. We added 28,000 net video subs, with 65% coming from upselling existing broadband customers via our AI-driven recommendation engine, which boosts attachment rates by 18%. Wireless residential adds of 19,000 reflect our 5G Home fixed-wireless access trials in rural markets, competing head-on with T-Mobile's 5G Home Internet; penetration here hit 15% in test markets like rural Pennsylvania, with ARPU premiums of $15 over traditional DSL.

Regionally, U.S. residential drove 78% of adds at 165,000, while Europe contributed 37,000—up 45% YoY—thanks to our Vodafone JV in Germany, where 5G SA standalone rollout enabled low-latency bundles with DAZN sports streaming. Latin America lagged slightly at 10,000 adds, impacted by FX volatility in Brazil, but our prepaid mobile-to-postpaid conversions improved 22% via zero-rating social media apps.

Shifting to business, we posted 36,000 net adds, a 22% QoQ increase and our best in two years, highlighting the enterprise shift to hybrid work and edge computing. Breakdown: Ethernet and fiber adds of 18,000, SD-WAN of 12,000, and voice/cloud UCaaS of 6,000. This segment's low churn of 0.8%—versus industry averages north of 2%—stems from our 400G wavelength services, now live in 15 metro markets, supporting hyperscalers like AWS and Google Cloud with sub-1ms latency.

Key wins included a multi-year deal with a Fortune 50 retailer for private 5G at 150 stores, adding 4,500 RGUs, and expanding our VeriEdge IoT platform to 25,000 business endpoints, up 40% YoY, powering smart factories akin to Verizon's 5G MEC deployments. In EMEA, business adds surged 55% to 14,000, led by UK public sector contracts for secure backhaul post-Brexit data sovereignty rules. APAC contributed modestly at 5,000, with upside from our NTT Docomo alliance targeting Japan enterprise 5G slicing.

Strategically, these results validate our 'Converge & Conquer' initiative: cross-selling media bundles to residential while layering AI orchestration—like our proprietary OSS/BSS upgrades—for business predictive maintenance, reducing downtime 30%. We've held post-price-increase churn flat at 1.4% residential, extracting 4% ARPU uplift without sacrificing volume. Looking ahead, Q4 guidance calls for 225,000 to 275,000 total net adds, with business accelerating to 40,000+ on 10,000 miles of additional fiber lit. Risks remain around spectrum auctions and regulatory noise in Europe, but our $2.5 billion capex plan—65% to fiber/5G—positions us for 2024 broadband-only growth of 20%+.

Next, I'd like to spend some time on one of our most valuable strategic assets: our spectrum portfolio. Spectrum remains the lifeblood of our wireless and converged media services here at VeriCom Global, powering everything from our nationwide 5G network to our Spectrum-branded fixed wireless access and low-latency streaming for sports and live events. Today, I'll cover current utilization metrics, emerging trends, and our forward-looking allocation strategy to drive sustainable growth in this hyper-competitive telecom and media landscape.

As of the end of Q3, our overall spectrum utilization stands at 82% across our licensed holdings, up from 74% a year ago and 68% two years back. This reflects the explosive demand we're seeing, particularly in mid-band C-band spectrum—where we're at 89% utilization in top-100 DMAs—and our low-band 600 MHz assets, humming along at 76%. For context, that's delivering spectral efficiency of 4.2 bits per Hertz in our 5G Standalone deployments, a 25% improvement YoY thanks to massive MIMO 64T64R configurations and AI-driven dynamic spectrum sharing.

Breaking it down by service: Mobile broadband traffic surged 48% YoY, with 5G accounting for 62% of total data volume—mirroring trends at peers like T-Mobile, which reported similar ramps post their 2.5 GHz refarming. Our fixed wireless access, or FWA, service now utilizes 35% of our mid-band capacity in suburban and rural overlays, serving 1.2 million households with median speeds of 450 Mbps down. That's clawing market share from cable rivals like Comcast in ex-urban markets, where we're pricing FWA at $50/month bundled with our ad-supported streaming tiers. Video delivery, critical for our media side, consumes about 22% of spectrum during peak hours, optimized via edge caching and multicast ABR streaming to handle UHD events like NFL Sunday Ticket equivalents without choking the pipe.

Regionally, utilization varies predictably. In the Northeast Corridor—New York to DC metro—we're pushing 95% on mmWave assets in dense urban cores, where enterprise private networks for stadiums and arenas are eating up 15% of that capacity. Think AR/VR media experiences at venues like Yankee Stadium partners. Conversely, in the Midwest and Southeast rural bands, utilization is at 65%, giving us ample headroom for FWA expansion amid the BEAD program's $42 billion rollout. Internationally, our AWSI licenses in the 3.45-3.55 GHz band are at 40% utilization but growing 30% QoQ as we test Open RAN pilots with Nokia and Rakuten Symphony.

We're in the midst of a multi-year spectrum crunch, exacerbated by 5G Advanced and the looming 6G horizon. Data from Ookla and Opensignal shows U.S. wireless data consumption up 35% YoY industry-wide, with video and gaming driving 55% of that. Our own network telemetry confirms this—average monthly data per user hit 28 GB, up from 19 GB last year—while ARPU from premium 5G plans rose 8% to $62. But efficiency gains are keeping pace: Cloud RAN deployments have boosted our throughput by 40% without incremental spectrum, and we're leveraging CBRS Band 48 for indoor enterprise meshing, much like Verizon's approach in verticals.

On the technical front, we're executing several initiatives to squeeze more value from existing holdings. First, spectrum refarming: By Q4, we'll reallocate 20 MHz of legacy 2G/3G 1900 MHz PCS spectrum to 5G NR in 40 underpenetrated markets, unlocking $150 million in incremental EBITDA over two years via higher ARPU tiers. Second, dynamic spectrum sharing trials between our C-band and 3.5 GHz pool are live in 15 cities, enabling seamless NSA-to-SA transitions and boosting peak-hour efficiency by 18%. We're also piloting network slicing for media workloads—allocating dedicated 100 MHz slices for low-latency 5G broadcast, partnering with the likes of Sinclair for ATSC 3.0 hybrids. And don't forget our mmWave investments: 45 GHz assets, acquired in the 2021 auction, are now at 12% utilization but poised for fixed-point-to-multipoint in enterprise media campuses.

Looking ahead to future allocation plans, our strategy is laser-focused on three pillars: monetization velocity, geographic arbitrage, and tech-led efficiency. Over the next 24 months, we'll allocate 60% of new capacity to consumer 5G Ultra and FWA growth, targeting 5 million FWA subs by 2026—directly competing with T-Mobile's aggressive pricing and Verizon's premium FWA push. Another 25% goes to enterprise and media verticals: Private 5G networks on CBRS and C-band slices for Hollywood studios' remote production and live esports streaming, where we're quoting $10,000/month per site with 99.9999% uptime SLAs. The remaining 15% is reserved for R&D, including 6G non-terrestrial network trials with Starlink interoperability.

Capex-wise, spectrum-related opex is flat at 12% of total, but we're earmarking $2.8 billion for 2025 densification—half in mid-band small cells, a quarter in fiber backhaul for edge compute. We'll participate selectively in future FCC auctions, prioritizing 3 GHz extensions and potential 7-8 GHz openings, while exploring secondary market trades like the recent Dish-Amazon deals. Partnerships are key: Our JV with Google Cloud for ORAN-based spectrum orchestration will cut vendor lock-in and enable AI predictive allocation, potentially saving 20% on future builds.

Strategically, this positions us ahead of the curve. While AT&T grapples with post-Warner divestitures and spectrum debt loads, and Charter focuses on DOCSIS 4.0 cable, our hybrid telco-media model lets us cross-leverage spectrum for Peacock-like streaming bundles, driving 15% blended ARPU uplift. Risks include regulatory headwinds like the FCC's C-band settlement delays that cost us $50 million last year—but our 1.2 GHz-POPs position gives us fortress-like coverage versus fiber-only upstarts.

Now, turning to our Content and Media segment, which continues to be a high-growth engine for VeriCom Global, powering our integrated telecom-media ecosystem. This quarter, the segment delivered robust results amid a dynamic landscape of streaming fragmentation, premium sports rights inflation, and accelerating ad market recovery.

Starting with revenue, we reported $2.85 billion in the quarter, up 12% year-over-year on a reported basis and 14% on a constant currency basis. This marks our ninth straight quarter of double-digit growth, outpacing the broader U.S. pay-TV market, which contracted 5% per Nielsen data, and even the OTT segment's 8% industry average as tracked by Ampere Analysis.

The growth was driven by a healthy mix: Subscription and licensing revenue of $1.72 billion, +10% YoY, fueled by our flagship GlobalStream OTT platform and bundling synergies with our 5G mobile and fiber broadband base—HBO Max-style premium bundles with our wireless plans added $250 million incrementally, similar to how Comcast's Xfinity Stream has stabilized linear declines. Advertising revenue of $850 million, +18% YoY, benefiting from the post-strike ad rebound and our connected TV inventory. AVOD tiers on GlobalStream, akin to Netflix's ad-supported plan, now represent 25% of new subs and drove $320 million—up 35%—thanks to targeted programmatic deals with The Trade Desk and Google's DV360. Content licensing and other at $280 million, +8% YoY, from syndicating originals like our 'NeoFrontiers' sci-fi franchise to international platforms such as Peacock and Paramount+.

Regionally, North America contributed 65% of revenue at $1.85 billion (+11% YoY), anchored by NFL Sunday Ticket renewals and March Madness integrations. EMEA grew 20% to $650 million, propelled by Premier League rights in the UK and Bundesliga expansions in Germany, despite regulatory headwinds from the DMA. APAC and LATAM added $350 million combined, up 15%, with strong traction in Brazil via Vivo bundles and India through Jio-like partnerships.

On profitability, segment Adjusted EBITDA reached $920 million, a +15% YoY increase, with margins expanding 180 basis points to 32.3%. This reflects disciplined cost management amid content amortization pressures. Key drivers included a 22% reduction in churn-related acquisition costs per sub, down to $45 from $58, via AI-driven personalization engines powered by our AWS-partnered recommendation algorithms—boosting retention by 15% for users engaged with hyper-personalized feeds. EBITDA margins in subscriptions held steady at 35%, while AVOD scaled to 28% margins, leveraging our edge CDN network co-located with 5G towers for sub-2-second latency, outcompeting legacy players like DirecTV. Content spend was $1.4 billion, flat YoY as a percentage of revenue at 49%, with 65% allocated to high-ROI originals and sports. We amortized $650 million in the quarter, but strategic shifts—like co-productions with Lionsgate—improved our library monetization by 12%. Challenges included a $50 million sports rights escalation for NBA extensions, but this is offset by 20% YoY uplift in sports streaming ARPU.

On subscriber metrics, we saw continued momentum: Total paid subscribers of 152.3 million, +2.8 million net adds quarter-over-quarter, marking our strongest Q3 since 2021. This compares favorably to Disney+'s 2.4 million global adds and Warner Bros. Discovery's flatline. GlobalStream direct-to-consumer: 98 million (+1.9 million net adds), with churn at a record-low 1.2% monthly, down from 1.8% YoY, thanks to family plan bundling and 4K/HDR upgrades. Wholesale and MVPD partnerships: 54.3 million (+900k adds), including carriage on Charter Spectrum and Cox, where we captured 70% of their video share. Blended ARPU: $6.25 per month, +4% YoY, driven by premium tier uptake (40% of base now on ad-free at $17.99) and upsell to sports add-ons ($9.99 NBA/NFL packs). Regional breakdown: North America at 105 million subs (+1.5 million adds), EMEA 32 million (+800k, led by Sky Deutschland growth), and Emerging Markets 15.3 million (+500k, with 25% QoQ acceleration in LATAM via Claro Video integrations).

Strategically, we're leaning into three initiatives: 5G-OTT Convergence, rolling out low-latency streaming over our mmWave network, targeting 50ms end-to-end for live events—piloted with Coachella broadcasts, aiming to add 10 million subs by year-end. AI and Data Flywheel via our proprietary 'MediaMind' platform, using federated learning across 200 million+ user sessions, has lifted content engagement 28%, directly correlating to 15% ARPU uplift in test markets. M&A and Partnerships: Post our acquisition of StreamCo's FAST channels, we're expanding free ad-supported TV to 50 channels by Q1 2025, while deepening bundling with telco peers like Vodafone in Europe to counter cord-cutting. Looking ahead, we guide Q4 segment revenue growth of 10-12% YoY, with EBITDA margins at 33%, assuming stable linear declines offset by streaming tailwinds. This positions Content and Media as 25% of our total EBITDA, up from 20% last year.

Finally, let's dive into the impact of our new product and service launches on revenue and subscriber growth. As you know, VeriCom Global is at the forefront of converging telecommunications and media, leveraging our nationwide 5G Standalone network, fiber-to-the-home footprint covering 45% of U.S. households, and our NexStream OTT platform. In Q3, these launches delivered a robust $478 million in incremental revenue—representing 12% of our total quarterly revenue—and drove net subscriber additions of 1.45 million across mobile, broadband, and media segments. This marks a 28% year-over-year increase in launch-attributable revenue and a 35% YoY surge in related subscriber growth, outpacing industry averages reported by peers like Verizon and Comcast.

First, our 5G Fixed Wireless Access Nationwide Rollout—'NexWave Home Ultra'. In June, we expanded FWA to 25 million U.S. homes and 8 million in Europe via our joint venture with Vodafone. This mid-band 5G C-band spectrum solution delivers symmetric gigabit speeds averaging 1.2 Gbps download, targeting underserved rural and suburban markets where FTTH economics are challenging. We've integrated Open RAN architecture for 30% lower capex per site, aligning with FCC auction trends. It generated $212 million in Q3, with 65% from new broadband subs and 35% from premium add-ons like 4K streaming optimization. This contributed to a 18% QoQ ARPU lift to $68/month for FWA customers. Subscriber growth added 825,000 broadband subscribers, a 42% YoY increase. Penetration hit 15% in launch markets, reducing our rural broadband churn by 2.2 percentage points to 1.1%. U.S. drove 72% of adds (595,000), fueled by T-Mobile-like competitive dynamics post-spectrum auctions. In Europe, 230,000 adds amid regulatory tailwinds from the EU's Gigabit Society initiative. FWA is our 'wireless-first' broadband play, capturing 22% market share in non-fiber ZIP codes per New Street Research data. It positions us to defend against cable giants like Charter, with projected $1.2 billion full-year run-rate by FY24.

Second, NexStream+ Bundle with Original Content and Cloud Gaming. Our July rebrand of NexStream integrated ad-supported original series (e.g., 'Quantum Edge' sci-fi thriller co-produced with Lionsgate) and Xbox Cloud Gaming via a Microsoft partnership. Priced at $15/month standalone or bundled free with premium mobile postpaid plans, it features AI-driven personalization using our edge computing nodes for <50ms latency. Revenue impact: $156 million incremental, with 55% from direct subscriptions, 30% from bundling uplift, and 15% from in-app ads/AVOD. Media segment ARPU rose 14% to $22/month. Subscriber growth: 420,000 net adds to NexStream (total base now 18.5 million), plus 185,000 upsells from mobile video bundles. Month-over-month growth of 8%, versus Netflix's 4% global average. Strong in North America (65% of adds, or 390,000), where cord-cutting accelerated 5% YoY per eMarketer. Asia-Pacific contributed 95,000 via our Singtel JV, tapping 5G gaming demand in markets like Indonesia. Bundling reduced overall churn by 1.5 points to 1.3%, mirroring Disney Bundle success at Hulu. With 5G SA enabling low-latency cloud gaming, we're targeting 25% media ARPU growth in 2024, countering pure-play streamers like Roku.

Third, Enterprise 5G Private Networks and Edge Media Services. August pilot expansions with Siemens for Industry 4.0 private 5G slices and media clients like ESPN for AR/VR live events. Leveraging our 2,500+ edge points of presence, these offer network slicing for ultra-reliable low-latency comms. Revenue impact: $110 million, primarily recurring from 5-year contracts; EBITDA margins at 52%, higher than consumer segments. Subscriber growth: 25,000 enterprise 'slices' activated, equivalent to 50,000 mobile-equivalent subs via multi-tenancy. U.S. (80% or $88 million) led by manufacturing hubs; EMEA added $18 million amid 5G SA mandates in Germany. This B2B pivot diversifies revenue, with 40% gross margins versus 35% consumer. It aligns with GSMA forecasts of $150 billion global private 5G TAM by 2028.

In aggregate, total revenue from launches: $478 million (+28% YoY), accelerating from $320 million in Q2. New launches boosted overall revenue growth to 7.2% YoY, offsetting legacy voice declines. Total subscribers: +1.45 million net adds (mobile: 650k; broadband: 550k; media: 250k). Postpaid mobile phone net adds hit 420k, with 5G penetration at 62%. Key trends: 5G adoption surged 15% QoQ, driving 11% ARPU expansion. Amid macroeconomic pressures like inflation impacting 10% of low-ARPU subs, bundles mitigated churn. Competitively, we're gaining 2 points of wireless market share per Fitch estimates, pressuring AT&T's mid-band lags. Forward guidance: We expect Q4 launch revenue of $550-600 million, with 1.7 million sub adds, supported by holiday 5G promotions and FTTH overbuilds to 55% U.S. coverage.

These launches underscore our 'Converged 5G Media' strategy: integrating spectrum assets, content IP, and edge tech to deliver sticky, high-margin growth. We're not just a telco—we're the media backbone of the 5G era.

Operator: Thank you. We will now begin the question-and-answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from Mike Thompson with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Mike Thompson: Good morning. Can you provide more color on the net subscriber trends in business and how spectrum utilization is influencing those adds?

Alex Rivera: Thanks, Mike. Happy to elaborate. As Jordan detailed, our business segment saw 36,000 net adds, up 22% quarter-over-quarter, driven by Ethernet, fiber, SD-WAN, and UCaaS. Our 82% spectrum utilization, especially the 89% in mid-band C-band, has been key, enabling 400G services and private 5G wins like the Fortune 50 retailer deal. This low churn at 0.8% positions us well for Q4's 40,000+ target.

Jordan Lee: To add, Mike, our refarming and DSS initiatives are directly fueling these, with headroom in rural bands for more FWA and enterprise slicing.

Operator: Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen: Hi, thanks for taking my question. Could you elaborate on your plans for content and media profitability and the revenue impact from new launches like NexStream+?

Jordan Lee: Absolutely, Lisa. Our content segment's 32.3% EBITDA margin expansion to $920 million came from cost efficiencies like 22% lower acquisition costs via AI personalization and scaled AVOD at 28% margins. For new launches, NexStream+ alone drove $156 million and 420,000 adds, with bundling lifting media ARPU 14%. We're guiding 10-12% Q4 growth there, leveraging 5G-OTT convergence.

Alex Rivera: And Lisa, this ties into our broader convergence, where media bundles are cross-selling effectively across residential and business.

Sarah Jenkins: Thank you for your questions. That concludes our Q&A session. Alex, would you like to provide closing remarks?

Alex Rivera: Thank you. In closing, I am proud of our team's performance this quarter. We are well-positioned to continue delivering value to our customers and shareholders with strong subscriber momentum, optimized spectrum use, thriving content performance, and innovative launches. Thank you for joining us today.

Operator: This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
